verses.text: E happen for di days wey di judges dey judge say famine dey for di land. One man of Bethlehem Judah go live for di country of Moab, with im wife and im two pikin man dem.
Di man name na Elimelech, im wife name na Naomi, and im two pikin man dem names na Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehem Judah. Dem come to di country of Moab, and live dere.
Elimelech, Naomi husband, die; and Naomi remain with im two pikin man dem.
Dem take wives for demself from di women of Moab. Di name of one na Orpah, and di name of di other na Ruth. Dem live dere about ten years.
Mahlon and Chilion die too, di two of dem; and di woman lose im two pikin dem and im husband.
Den e rise with im two pikin wife dem, so that e go return from di country of Moab; because e don hear for di country of Moab how di Lord visit im people, give dem bread.
E go out from di place wia e dey, and im two pikin wife dem with am; and dem dey waka for di road to return to di land of Judah.
Naomi talk to im two pikin wife dem say, “Go, return, every one of una to di house of im mama. Make di Lord show una kindness, as una don show to di dead and to me.
Make di Lord grant una say una go find rest, every one for di house of im husband.” Den e kiss dem, and dem lift up dem voice, and weep.
Dem talk to am say, “No, but we go return with you to your people.”
Naomi talk say, “Go back, my pikin woman dem. Why una go follow me? I still get pikin man dem for my womb, so that dem go become una husbands?
Go back, my pikin woman dem, go una way; because I too old to get husband. If I talk say, ‘I get hope,’ if even I get husband tonight, and still born pikin man dem,
una go wait for dem until dem grow? Una go stop to get husbands for dem? No, my pikin woman dem, because e dey pain me seriously for una sake, because di Lord hand don go out against me.”
Dem lift up dem voice, and weep again: and Orpah kiss im mama-in-law; but Ruth stay with am.
E talk say, “Look, your sister-in-law don go back to im people, and to im god. Follow your sister-in-law.”
Ruth talk say, “No press me to leave you, and to return from following you, because wia you go, I go go; and wia you stay, I go stay. Your people go be my people, and your God my God.
Wia you die, I go die, and dere dem go bury me. Make di Lord do so to me, and more also, if anything except death separate you and me.”
When Naomi see say Ruth don make up im mind to go with am, e stop to speak to am.
So di two of dem go until dem reach Bethlehem. When dem reach Bethlehem, all di city stir because of dem, and dem talk say, “Na Naomi be dis?”
E talk to dem say, “No call me Naomi. Call me Mara; because di Almighty don deal with me very bitterly.
I go out full, and di Lord don bring me come home empty. Why una dey call me Naomi, since di Lord don testify against me, and di Almighty don afflict me?”
So Naomi return, and Ruth di Moabitess, im pikin wife, with am, wey return from di country of Moab: and dem reach Bethlehem for di beginning of barley harvest.
Naomi get one relative of im husband, one mighty man of wealth, from di family of Elimelech, and im name na Boaz.
Ruth di Moabitess talk to Naomi say, “Make I go to di field now, and glean di ears of grain after anybody wey I go find favour for im eyes.” E talk to am say, “Go, my pikin woman.”
E go, come glean for di field after di reapers: and e happen reach di part of di field wey belong to Boaz, wey be from di family of Elimelech.
Look, Boaz come from Bethlehem, and talk to di reapers say, “Di Lord dey with una.” Dem answer am say, “Make di Lord bless you.”
Den Boaz talk to im servant wey dem put over di reapers say, “Na whose young woman be dis?”
Di servant wey dem put over di reapers answer say, “Na di Moabite young woman wey come back with Naomi from di country of Moab.
E talk say, ‘Please make I glean and gather after di reapers among di sheaves.’ So e come, and e don dey dere from morning till now, except say e rest small for di house.”
Den Boaz talk to Ruth say, “Listen, my pikin woman. No go glean for another field, and no go away from here, but stay here near my young women.

Make your eyes dey for di field wey dem dey reap, and follow dem. I no command di young men say dem no go touch you? When you dey thirsty, go to di vessels, and drink from wetin di young men don draw.”
Den e fall on im face, bow to di ground, and talk to am say, “Why I find favour for your eyes, say you notice me, since I na foreigner?”

Boaz answer am say, “Dem don tell me everything wey you do to your mama-in-law since di death of your husband, and how you leave your papa and your mama and di land wia dem born you, and come to people wey you no know before.
Make di Lord pay you for your work, and make full reward dey given to you from di Lord, God of Israel, under whose wings you don come take refuge.”
Den e talk say, “Make I find favour for your eyes, my oga, because you don comfort me, and because you speak kindly to your servant, even though I no be like one of your servants.”

For meal time Boaz talk to am say, “Come here, eat some bread, and dip your piece for di vinegar.” Ruth sit beside di reapers, and Boaz give am roasted grain, and e eat until e satisfy, and e leave some.
When e rise up to glean, Boaz command im young men, talk say, “Make am glean even among di sheaves, and no disgrace am.
Also pull out some for am from di bundles, and leave am, make am glean, and no rebuke am.”
So e glean for di field until evening; and e beat out wetin e glean, and e be about one ephah of barley.
E carry am up, go inside di city, and im mama-in-law see wetin e glean. E bring out and give am wetin e leave after e satisfy.

Im mama-in-law talk to am say, “Wia you glean today? Wia you work? Make di one wey notice you get blessing.” E show im mama-in-law di person wey e work with, and talk say, “Di name of di man wey I work with today na Boaz.”
Naomi talk to im pikin wife say, “Make di Lord bless am, wey no forsake im kindness to di living and to di dead.” Naomi talk to am say, “Di man na our close relative, one of our redeemers.”
Ruth di Moabitess talk say, “Yes, e talk to me say, ‘You go stay near my young men, until dem finish all my harvest.’”
Naomi talk to Ruth im pikin wife say, “E good, my pikin woman, say you go out with im young women, so that dem no go meet you for any other field.”
So e stay near di young women of Boaz to glean till di end of barley harvest and wheat harvest; and e dey live with im mama-in-law.
Naomi, im mama-in-law, talk to am say, “My pikin woman, I no go seek rest for you, so that e go dey well with you?
Now Boaz no be our relative, wey you dey with im young women? Look, e dey winnow barley tonight for di threshing floor.
So wash yourself, anoint yourself, put on your best clothes, and go down to di threshing floor, but no make yourself known to di man until e finish to eat and drink.
E go be say, when e lie down, you go note di place wia e lie down, and you go go in, uncover im feet, and lie down; and e go tell you wetin to do.”
E talk to am say, “All wetin you talk, I go do.”
E go down to di threshing floor, and do everything wey im mama-in-law tell am.
When Boaz don eat and drink, and im heart merry, e go lie down for di end of di heap of grain; and Ruth come softly, uncover im feet, and lie down.
E happen for midnight, say di man shake and turn imself; and look, one woman dey lie for im feet.
E talk, “Who be you?” E answer, “I na Ruth your servant. Spread your cloak over your servant; because you na redeemer.”
E talk say, “Blessing from di Lord dey on you, my pikin woman. You show more kindness for di end pass di beginning, because you no follow young men, whether poor or rich.
Now, my pikin woman, no fear. I go do to you all wetin you talk; because all di city of my people know say you na virtuous woman.
Now na true say I na redeemer; but one redeemer dey wey near pass me.

Stay dis night, and for morning, if e go do for you di duty of redeemer, e good; make am do di duty of redeemer. But if e no wan do di duty of redeemer for you, den I go do di duty of redeemer for you, as di Lord dey live. Lie down till morning.”
E lie for im feet till morning, and e rise before one person fit recognise another. Because Boaz talk say, “Make dem no know say di woman come to di threshing floor.”
E talk say, “Bring di cloak wey dey on you, and hold am.” Ruth hold am; and Boaz measure six measures of barley, and put am on Ruth; den Boaz go inside di city.
When Ruth reach im mama-in-law, Naomi talk say, “Who be you, my pikin woman?” Ruth tell am all wetin di man do for am.
E talk say, “E give me dis six measures of barley; because e talk say, ‘No go empty to your mama-in-law.’”
Den Naomi talk say, “Sit still, my pikin woman, until you know how di matter go end; because di man no go rest, until e finish di thing today.”
Now Boaz go up to di gate, and sit down dere: and look, di redeemer wey Boaz speak about pass; and Boaz talk to am say, “Come here, my friend, and sit down!” E come, and sit down.
Boaz take ten men from di elders of di city, and talk say, “Sit down here,” and dem sit down.
E talk to di redeemer say, “Naomi, wey don come back from di country of Moab, dey sell di piece of land wey belong to our brother Elimelech.

I think say I go tell you, talk say, ‘Buy am before di people wey dey sit here, and before di elders of my people.’ If you go redeem am, redeem am; but if you no go redeem am, den tell me, so that I go know; because nobody dey wey go redeem am except you; and I dey after you.” E talk say, “I go redeem am.”
Den Boaz talk say, “For di day wey you buy di field from Naomi hand, you must buy am from Ruth di Moabitess too, di wife of di dead man, to raise up di name of di dead man for im inheritance.”
Di redeemer talk say, “I no fit redeem am for myself, because I fit spoil my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption for yourself; because I no fit redeem am.”

Now dis na di custom for former time for Israel about redeeming and about exchanging, to confirm all things: one man dey take off im shoe, dey give am to im neighbour; and na dis be di way to confirm things for Israel.
So di redeemer talk to Boaz say, “Buy am for yourself.” E take off im shoe.
Boaz talk to di elders, and to all di people say, “Una be witnesses today, say I don buy all wetin belong to Elimelech, and all wetin belong to Chilion and Mahlon, from Naomi hand.

Moreover Ruth di Moabitess, di wife of Mahlon, I don buy am to be my wife, to raise up di name of di dead man for im inheritance, so that di name of di dead man no go cut off from among im brothers, and from di gate of im place. Una be witnesses today.”

All di people wey dey di gate, and di elders, talk say, “We be witnesses. Make di Lord make di woman wey don come into your house like Rachel and like Leah, wey both build di house of Israel; and make you prosper for Ephrathah, and make your name famous for Bethlehem.
Make your house be like di house of Perez, wey Tamar born for Judah, because of di offspring wey di Lord go give you through dis young woman.”
So Boaz take Ruth, and e become im wife; and e sleep with am, and di Lord enable am to conceive, and e born one pikin man.
Di women talk to Naomi say, “Make dem bless di Lord, wey no leave you today without one redeemer. Make im name famous for Israel.
E go be to you one wey go restore your life, and sustain you for your old age, because your pikin wife, wey love you, wey better to you pass seven pikin man dem, don born am.”
Naomi take di pikin, put am for im bosom, and become nurse to am.
Di women, im neighbours, give am name, talk say, “One pikin man don born for Naomi.” Dem name am Obed. E na di papa of Jesse, wey be di papa of David.
Now dis na di generations of Perez: Perez born Hezron,
and Hezron born Ram, and Ram born Amminadab,
and Amminadab born Nahshon, and Nahshon born Salmon,
and Salmon born Boaz, and Boaz born Obed,
and Obed born Jesse, and Jesse born David.
